title: Isotopic Ratios in the Disk of HD 163296
question: Can rare CO isotopologue observations in an optically thin outer disk region beyond a sharp CO snowline empirically constrain carbon and oxygen isotopic ratios without detailed disk modeling?

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image native 13C18O(2-1) and verify Keplerian kinematics
recipe.method: Standard pipeline calibration, self-calibration, tclean imaging with Briggs robust 0.5 to 3-sigma threshold, JvM and primary beam correction; generate moment-0 and moment-1 maps using bettermoments with 2-sigma clip
key_parameters: robust = 0.5, 3-sigma CLEAN threshold, 0.28'' x 0.25'' beam, 2-sigma intensity clip for moments

recipe.goal: Reimage all four transitions to a common circularized beam and extract radial intensity and ratio profiles
recipe.method: Reimage C17O(1-0), C18O(1-0), 13C18O(2-1), and C17O(2-1) with robust 0.5 and uv taper to a common 0.52'' circularized beam with JvM and PB corrections; extract deprojected azimuthally averaged radial profiles using GoFish radial_profile
key_parameters: common circularized beam FWHM = 0.52'', robust = 0.5, 7.1% systematic uncertainty added in quadrature for Band 6 ratio
assumptions: 5% absolute flux calibration uncertainty per dataset; Band 3 lines share common flux scale (correlated, rho ~ 1); Band 6 datasets assumed uncorrelated (rho = 0) worst case

recipe.goal: Quantify same-transition isotopologue flux ratios as a function of optical depth using non-LTE radiative transfer grids
recipe.method: Run non-LTE radiative transfer calculations over a grid of T_kin, n_H2, and N_CO using RADEX via SpectralRadex to compute line-center optical depth and flux ratios
assumptions: Ortho-to-para H2 ratio of 3:1; CMB background T_bg = 2.73 K; canonical ISM isotopic ratios: 12C/13C = 69, 16O/18O = 557, 18O/17O = 3.6

recipe.goal: Constrain carbon and oxygen isotopic ratios at r = 1.5'' using MCMC fitting of beam-averaged line intensities
recipe.method: Extract beam-averaged integrated intensities in an annulus centered at 1.5'' and fit them using an MCMC approach (emcee) coupled with RADEX over 7 free parameters
key_parameters: Annulus centered at 1.5'' (~150 au), smoothed over 0.52'' beam; 7 free parameters
assumptions: Single uniform slab at 1.5'' where Delta V represents local thermal plus microturbulent FWHM

answer_key.quantity: CO snowline radius (local minimum of radial derivative)

evidence.quote: The intensity decreases smoothly with radius, and the derivative exhibits a clear local minimum at 0.75$''$, coincident with the CO snowline radius inferred from other CO isotopologues (cite: Qi2024).

Both the C$^{17}$O/$^{13}$C$^{18}$O(2–1) and C$^{18}$O/C$^{17}$O(1–0) flux ratios rise sharply across the CO snowline and flatten beyond 1.5$''$ ($r \gtrsim 150$ au), where the emission becomes optically thin.
The C$^{17}$O/$^{13}$C$^{18}$O(2–1) ratio approaches approximately 20, consistent with the ISM value expected under optically thin emission conditions for both lines
while the C$^{18}$O/C$^{17}$O(1–0) ratio stabilizes near 2.7, implying moderate optical depth in the C$^{18}$O(1–0) line for ISM-like abundances

score_reason: The core analysis (RADEX + emcee MCMC on the four beam-averaged fluxes in Table 1) is completely specified with explicit priors, molecular data sources, and tabular inputs/outputs, making the radiative transfer and MCMC steps immediately reproducible. The visibility imaging and GoFish profile extraction steps lose a few points because self-cal details are deferred to a companion paper and exact deprojection/uv-taper parameters are not explicitly listed.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the software stack (CASA, GoFish, bettermoments, SpectralRadex/RADEX, emcee) is standard and open-source, intermediate integrated intensities at 1.5'' are explicitly tabulated in Table 1, and the main scientific results are precise numeric isotopic ratios in Table 2.
